spans.text: The open marketplace where production-ready AI agents are published, discovered, and deployed in one click.
Welcome to the documentation hub for

— the open agent marketplace for the [&] Protocol ecosystem. FleetPrompt is the registry where production-ready AI agents are published, discovered, and deployed. Every listed agent carries a versioned manifest, a computed trust score, declared permissions, and a linked SpecPrompt spec — making FleetPrompt the first marketplace where you know exactly what an agent does before you install it.
57% of organizations now have AI agents in production (LangChain 2026). Yet there are

. Teams build agents in isolation, rediscover the same patterns, and have no way to share, reuse, or monetize production-quality work. Closed platforms (Salesforce AgentForce, OpenAI GPT Store) lock agents into proprietary runtimes. Open frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI) have no distribution story at all.

spans.text: — Every agent defined by a machine-readable manifest. No opaque binaries. 2.
— Trust scores derived from tests, audits, and usage — never self-reported. 3.
— All permissions declared upfront, reviewed on install. 4.
— Every version links to its SpecPrompt spec, build pipeline, and audit trail. 5.
— Install means deploy to OpenSentience. No manual wiring. 6.
— Public agents are free to publish and install. The marketplace is the commons. 7.
— Any public agent can be forked, customized, and republished.
Manifest storage, version control, search indexing, fork management
Async recompute of trust scores on new data
Manifest → OpenSentience deploy with permission review gate
Agent search, detail, trust scores, publisher profiles
Every agent on FleetPrompt gets a computed trust score based on:
— percentage of acceptance criteria with passing tests
— install count, active deployments, error rates
— linked SpecPrompt spec, Agentelic build history
Trust scores are recomputed asynchronously whenever new data arrives.
